scope.description: The two-mode five-node restart scenario (feature-on restart and feature-off control in one execution) with the healed phase extended into a long run of 200 further committed entries before the sample.
assumptions: All state is produced by normal operations: bootstrap {A,B,C}, election, committed applies, a user snapshot on A, AddVoter D and E, graceful restart of A with and without the feature, transport partition, healing and further committed entries.

The long run is applied on the healed leader whichever node it is; in the feature-on run that leader may be the stale node, in which case its own configuration decides which peers receive the entries, which is recorded through the per-node log indexes.
The sample is taken after the leader's log has advanced at least 150 entries past the conflict index, with a 15s bound; the derived long_run_exercised operand states whether that happened.
Exact indexes are not asserted; the comparisons use the mode-conditioned structural operands.
excluded: No crash, on-disk store or user Restore is exercised.
The long run commits ordinary command entries only; no further membership change is made during it.

basis.prefix: The helper builds five InmemTransports in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore and Config with TrailingLogs 0, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and the feature enabled, elects a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits for A to apply, takes a user snapshot on A, starts D and E, adds each as voter, applies one further command and emits 'fixture'. It shuts A down, cuts {A,C} from {B,D,E}, reconnects A to C only, restarts A with the mode's feature setting and emits 'restart'. It waits for a leader in each partition, applies one write on each leader, reads the entries at the shared index and emits 'outcome'. It reconnects the mesh, waits for one leader, applies one more entry, then applies 200 further entries on that leader and waits (bounded by 15s) until the leader's log has advanced at least 150 entries past the conflict index; only then does it sample payloads and terms at the conflict index, differences in the applied write lists, each node's configuration and the long-run operands, and emit 'healed'. A repair phase follows as before: choose a current-configuration leader, cut A off, apply ten commands, snapshot the leader, reconnect A, wait for the snapshot install and emit 'repaired'. The test runs mode defect_restart first and control_no_restore second. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome, healed, repaired, fixture, restart, outcome, healed, repaired.

before.description: The five-node restart scenario (bootstrap {A,B,C}, committed applies, user snapshot on A, AddVoter D and E, graceful shutdown of A, partition {A,C} | {B,D,E}, restart of A, healing, repair by snapshot install) executed twice in one run: once restarting A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and once restarting it with the feature off, everything else identical, including that both runs stage the commit index during the first life by running with the feature enabled before the restart.
assumptions: Both runs use freshly created stores and transports; the mode is the only intended difference, and in both runs A's first life runs with the feature enabled so a persisted commit index exists.
The partition, healing and repair phases run identically in both modes; the repair phase triggers a snapshot install in both runs because the leader compacts while the restarted node is cut off.

Recorded rather than asserted: the applied-write metric across nodes is only meaningful when both sides committed a write, so the control comparisons use the restarted node's own applied writes and the leader counts instead of cluster-wide consistency.
excluded: No crash, on-disk store or user Restore is exercised.
The control reproduces the same first-life and partition schedule; it is a control for the restart mode, not for the scenario.
